title: vega-mir: An information-theoretic Python toolkit for symbolic music, with applications to harmonic graphs and rubato spectra
summary: We present vega-mir, an open-source Python library that bundles nine information-theoretic and statistical metrics for the analysis of symbolic music corpora behind a small, tested, citable API, and demonstrates two of them at corpus scale in case studies not addressed by the upstream Cygnus paper. Of the nine metrics, three (Shannon entropy, Kullback-Leibler divergence, Zipfian fits) were deployed in the companion Cygnus arXiv preprint; two (network analysis on chord-transition graphs and spectral analysis of rubato curves) are deployed in full case studies here; the four remaining (multi-dimensional Gini, chi-squared stationarity, Higuchi fractal dimension, interval distribution) are validated against analytic anchors and exercised as sanity checks on a bundled 8-composer dataset. The two case studies yield two main observations. First, on the fourteen MAESTRO composers with N >= 10 pieces, the PageRank value of the gravity-centre node correlates with the marginal Kullback-Leibler distance at rho = 0.61 (Spearman, composer-level jackknife N = 14); the categorical gravity-centre identity takes five distinct values across the corpus but is not itself correlated with marginal KL (rho = 0.13, p = 0.21). Second, on the 247-piece Bach multi-master corpus (Schiff, Gould, Richter), Gould holds the highest periodicity ratio of the three performers, not the lowest, inverting the cliché that low scalar rubato reads as "metronomic": Gould's rubato is small in amplitude but structured in time, with a median dominant period of 66 beats against Schiff's 102 and Richter's 104.

AI.tldr: vega-mir is an open-source Python library bundling nine information-theoretic and statistical metrics for symbolic music analysis, demonstrated through two case studies: (1) PageRank of gravity-centre nodes correlates with marginal KL divergence across MAESTRO composers (rho=0.61), and (2) Gould's rubato has the highest periodicity ratio among Bach performers, contradicting the "metronomic" cliché.
AI.motivation: To provide a tested, citable, open-source library of information-theoretic and statistical metrics for symbolic music corpora analysis, and to demonstrate these metrics at corpus scale in case studies that extend beyond the upstream Cygnus paper.
AI.method: Nine metrics were bundled: Shannon entropy, Kullback-Leibler divergence, Zipfian fits, network analysis on chord-transition graphs, spectral analysis of rubato curves, multi-dimensional Gini, chi-squared stationarity, Higuchi fractal dimension, and interval distribution. Two case studies were conducted: (1) PageRank vs. marginal KL on MAESTRO composers, and (2) periodicity ratio analysis on Bach multi-performer rubato curves.
AI.result: Case study 1: PageRank of gravity-centre node correlates with marginal KL at rho=0.61 (Spearman, N=14); categorical gravity-centre identity is not correlated (rho=0.13, p=0.21). Case study 2: Gould has the highest periodicity ratio (median dominant period 66 beats) vs. Schiff (102) and Richter (104), inverting the "metronomic" cliché.
AI.conclusion: vega-mir enables reproducible symbolic music analysis. The case studies reveal that network centrality (PageRank) relates to information-theoretic divergence, and that low-amplitude rubato can be highly structured in time rather than simply "metronomic."

title: S2Accompanist: A Semantic-Aware and Structure-Guided Diffusion Model for Music Accompaniment Generation
summary: High-fidelity text-to-music generation typically relies on massive proprietary datasets and immense computational resources. Existing models often struggle to generate coherent pure musical accompaniments and lack precise, localized semantic control due to their reliance on coarse, track-level annotations. To address these limitations under constrained data and computing resources, we propose S2Accompanist, a Semantic-Aware and Structure-Guided Diffusion Model developed for the ICME2026 ATTM Grand Challenge. Specifically, we design an automated data pipeline comprising structural segmentation, Large Audio-Language Model driven segment-level captioning, and dual-metric quality grading to overcome the absence of localized metadata in raw datasets. Furthermore, we propose a semantic-aware Variational Autoencoder fine-tuning strategy that explicitly distills foundational LeadSheet structures into the acoustic latent space, effectively improving the overall audio fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that S2Accompanist achieves state-of-the-art objective performance on the ATTM Grand Challenge benchmark across both the Efficiency and Performance Tracks. With only 402M parameters, our model remains competitive compared to larger-scale unconstrained models and secured first place in the Efficiency Track.

AI.tldr: S2Accompanist is a lightweight (402M params) semantic-aware, structure-guided diffusion model for text-to-music generation that uses an automated data pipeline (segmentation, LALM captioning, dual-metric grading) and a semantic-aware VAE fine-tuning strategy to achieve state-of-the-art performance on the ATTM Grand Challenge despite limited data and compute.
AI.motivation: Existing text-to-music models rely on massive proprietary datasets and compute, struggle to generate coherent pure accompaniments, and lack precise localized semantic control due to coarse track-level annotations. The goal is to overcome these limitations under constrained data and computing resources.
AI.method: (1) An automated data pipeline: structural segmentation, Large Audio-Language Model (LALM) driven segment-level captioning, dual-metric quality grading. (2) A semantic-aware VAE fine-tuning strategy that distills foundational LeadSheet structures into the acoustic latent space. (3) A semantic-aware and structure-guided diffusion model (S2Accompanist).
AI.result: State-of-the-art objective performance on ATTM Grand Challenge across both Efficiency and Performance Tracks. With only 402M parameters, remains competitive with larger unconstrained models and secured first place in the Efficiency Track.
AI.conclusion: S2Accompanist effectively addresses data and compute constraints through its automated pipeline and semantic-aware VAE fine-tuning, achieving SOTA results with a lightweight architecture, demonstrating that high-fidelity music generation is feasible without massive resources.

title: Audio-Image Cross-Modal Retrieval with Onomatopoeic Images
summary: Finding sound effects or environmental sounds that match a creator's intended impression remains a largely manual process in multimedia production. This is especially relevant for comics and other visual media, where visually stylized onomatopoeic expressions convey auditory impressions through letter shapes, strokes, layouts, and decorative patterns. However, cross-modal retrieval between onomatopoeic images and general sounds has been largely unexplored. This paper thus introduces a bidirectional retrieval framework between onomatopoeic images and the corresponding sound clips. Instead of directly comparing embeddings extracted from pretrained image and audio encoder, we train modality-specific projection heads that re-align the embeddings for visual onomatopoeia and corresponding sounds. We then construct the Multimodal Image-Audio Onomatopoeia dataset (MIAO), which contains paired onomatopoeic images and sound clips across 50 sound event classes. Experimental results show that the proposed method substantially outperforms a zero-shot baseline using pretrained CLIP and CLAP embeddings. These results demonstrate that adapting pretrained representations enables effective retrieval in both directions: from onomatopoeic images to sounds and from sounds to onomatopoeic images.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a bidirectional retrieval framework between onomatopoeic images and sound clips, using modality-specific projection heads to re-align pretrained embeddings, and constructs the MIAO dataset (50 sound event classes). The method significantly outperforms zero-shot baselines using CLIP/CLAP.
AI.motivation: Finding sounds matching a creator's intended impression in multimedia production (especially comics with stylized onomatopoeia) is still largely manual, and cross-modal retrieval between onomatopoeic images and general sounds has been largely unexplored.
AI.method: A bidirectional retrieval framework with modality-specific projection heads that re-align embeddings from pretrained image and audio encoders, plus construction of the MIAO dataset (paired onomatopoeic images and sound clips across 50 sound event classes).
AI.result: The proposed method substantially outperforms a zero-shot baseline using pretrained CLIP and CLAP embeddings on bidirectional retrieval tasks.
AI.conclusion: Adapting pretrained representations via modality-specific projection heads enables effective bidirectional retrieval between onomatopoeic images and corresponding sounds.

title: A Coupled Inductor Based Multi Port DC DC Converter with Coordinated Duty-Cycle and Phase Shift Control
summary: Electrified powertrains rely heavily on magnetics for power conversion, where cost, volume, and weight concerns make integrated multi-use designs an attractive solution. With EV powertrain architectures requiring a boost stage being a major market segment, the proposed Coupled Inductor-Based Multi-Port DC-DC Converter (CI-MPC) leverages the existing magnetic framework of a conventional topology to realize independent, isolated, and simultaneously regulated converters without additional magnetic cores or cascaded stages. Unlike existing architectures that use secondary windings solely for voltage gain or passive rectification, the proposed topology integrates an actively controlled full bridge on the secondary side to create a distinct, independently regulated auxiliary converter. Primary output regulation is achieved via duty-cycle control, while the auxiliary converter employs phase-shift modulation synchronized with the primary switching to enable active rectification and flexible voltage or current regulation. A unified control framework ensures decoupled operation with minimal interaction between the primary and auxiliary loops, while also avoiding high step-down conversion ratios from high voltages to lower auxiliary levels. The operating principles and coordinated control strategies are validated through simulation and experimental results on a hardware prototype, demonstrating enhanced controllability, decoupled regulation, and a scalable pathway toward generalized multi-port power conversion within a unified magnetic framework.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Coupled Inductor-Based Multi-Port DC-DC Converter (CI-MPC) that integrates an actively controlled secondary-side full bridge into a conventional coupled-inductor topology, enabling independent, isolated, and simultaneously regulated primary and auxiliary outputs from a single magnetic core without cascaded stages.
AI.motivation: Electrified powertrains demand cost, volume, and weight reductions in magnetics for power conversion, motivating integrated multi-use designs to avoid additional magnetic cores or cascaded converter stages.
AI.method: The CI-MPC adds an actively controlled full bridge on the secondary side of a coupled inductor topology. Primary output uses duty-cycle control; auxiliary output uses phase-shift modulation synchronized with primary switching for active rectification. A unified control framework decouples the two regulation loops.
AI.result: Simulation and experimental hardware validation demonstrate enhanced controllability, decoupled regulation between primary and auxiliary ports, and avoidance of high step-down conversion ratios, confirming the feasibility of the approach.
AI.conclusion: The proposed CI-MPC provides a scalable pathway toward generalized multi-port power conversion within a unified magnetic framework, suitable for EV powertrain applications requiring a boost stage.

title: MusicSynth: An Automated Pipeline for Generating Violin Fingerboard Animations from Sheet Music Using Optical Music Recognition
summary:
Learning the violin is harder than it looks. Unlike piano keys or guitar frets, the violin neck has no markings at all, so a beginner cannot tell by looking where to place each finger. MusicSynth is an open-source web tool that tries to fix that: user uploads a photo of any violin sheet music (or a digital score file), and the system automatically produces a video showing a violin fingerboard with each note highlighted at the right moment -- no software to install, no manual note entry required.
  The system connects three existing open-source tools into one pipeline: an optical music recognition (OMR) library reads the notes from the uploaded image, a MusicXML parser extracts timing information from digital scores, and a video renderer draws the fingerboard frame by frame. The only part built from scratch is the lookup table that maps each musical note to a string and finger position on the violin.
  Tested across 110 public-domain violin scores, MusicSynth correctly identified 91.2\,\% of notes in clean printed music and assigned the right finger position 99.1\,\% of the time when given a digital score file. To the author's knowledge, no freely available tool currently turns a sheet music image into an animated violin fingerboard tutorial automatically and in a single browser-based step.

AI.tldr: MusicSynth is an open-source web tool that converts violin sheet music (image or digital score) into an animated fingerboard video with highlighted notes, achieving 91.2% note accuracy on printed music and 99.1% correct finger placement on digital scores.
AI.motivation: The violin lacks visual markings (unlike piano or guitar), making it difficult for beginners to know where to place fingers. Existing tools require manual note entry or software installation, creating a barrier for learners.
AI.method: Connects three open-source tools: OMR library for note recognition from images, MusicXML parser for timing extraction from digital scores, and a video renderer for fingerboard animation. A custom lookup table maps notes to violin string/finger positions.
AI.result: 91.2% note identification accuracy on clean printed music, 99.1% correct finger position assignment from digital scores, tested on 110 public-domain violin scores.
AI.conclusion: MusicSynth is the first freely available, browser-based tool that automatically converts sheet music images into animated violin fingerboard tutorials without manual note entry or software installation.

title: Fractional-Order Subband p-Norm Adaptive Filter via Transformation Nearest Kronecker Product Decomposition for Active Noise Control
summary: The conventional normalized subband p-norm (NSPN) algorithm achieves robustness in $α$-stable noise ($1<α\leq 2$) by utilizing low-order error moments. However, its performance degrades significantly under three scenarios: (1) non-Gaussian inputs, (2) $α$-stable noise with $0<α\leq 1$, and (3) sparse system identification. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a fractional-order NSPN algorithm based on the nearest Kronecker product (NKP) decomposition and fractional-order stochastic gradient descent, termed NKP-FoNSPN. Theoretical bounds for the fractional-order parameter $β$ are also derived. Notably, when $β=1$, the NKP-FoNSPN reduces to a new NKP-NSPN algorithm, while its non-NKP decomposition variant becomes the fractional-order NSPN (FoNSPN) algorithm. Furthermore, a novel transformation-based NKP (TNKP) decomposition technique is designed, which exhibits lower computational complexity than conventional NKP for specific filter structures. The resulting TNKP-based FoNSPN (TNKP-FoNSPN) achieves lower steady-state misadjustment and multiplication cost compared with the NKP-FoNSPN algorithm. Additionally, complete computational complexity analyses are provided. For active noise control (ANC) scenarios, we develop filtered-x variants: NKP-FxFoNSPN and TNKP-FxFoNSPN. From the former, two additional variants are derived: NKP-FxNSPN and FxFoNSPN. Simulations using diverse noise sources (pink, helicopter, gunshot, pile driver, and traction substation noise) demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithms. Finally, we validate their noise reduction performance in a real constructed single-channel duct ANC and a simulated multi-channel ANC systems.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes fractional-order NSPN algorithms (NKP-FoNSPN, TNKP-FoNSPN, and filtered-x variants) using NKP decomposition and fractional-order SGD to improve robustness in α-stable noise with 0<α≤1, non-Gaussian inputs, and sparse system identification, validated through simulations and real ANC experiments.
AI.motivation: The conventional NSPN algorithm fails in three scenarios: non-Gaussian inputs, α-stable noise with 0<α≤1, and sparse system identification.
AI.method: Proposes fractional-order NSPN algorithm based on nearest Kronecker product (NKP) decomposition and fractional-order stochastic gradient descent, plus a transformation-based NKP (TNKP) decomposition for lower complexity.
AI.result: Simulations with diverse noise sources show superiority; real single-channel duct ANC and simulated multi-channel ANC validate noise reduction performance.
AI.conclusion: The proposed NKP-FoNSPN, TNKP-FoNSPN, and their filtered-x variants effectively address the limitations of conventional NSPN, achieving robustness and lower computational cost.

title: Health-Aware Fast Charging Using Homogenized Model with Heterogeneous Internal State Reconstruction
comment: 6 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for presentation at the IFAC World Congress 2026; to appear in IFAC-PapersOnLine
summary: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is limited by lithium plating, which occurs when the anode potential drops below 0 V vs Li/Li+. Model-based control aims to maximize charging current while maintaining anode potentials above this threshold. In this work, a plating-free fast charging strategy is demonstrated using a Homogenized Model (HM) coupled with a classical PID controller. The HM, derived from homogenization theory applied to the Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations, retains the physics of the Doyle-Fuller-Newman model while capturing electrode microstructural heterogeneity in a one-dimensional double-continua formulation. By reconstructing three-dimensional distributions of electrochemical variables from precomputed closure variables, the HM enables non-invasive estimation of heterogeneous anode potentials, acting as a virtual sensor. Through MATLAB-COMSOL co-simulation, a PID controller regulates current to maintain the full 3D anode potential distribution above the plating limit, achieving model-based fast charging at a fraction of the computational cost of high-fidelity models. The results demonstrate the potential of HM-based control for safe, degradation-aware, and efficient fast charging of lithium-ion batteries.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates a plating-free fast charging strategy for lithium-ion batteries using a Homogenized Model (HM) coupled with a PID controller. The HM, derived from homogenization theory applied to the Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations, captures electrode microstructural heterogeneity in a 1D double-continua formulation and enables non-invasive estimation of 3D heterogeneous anode potentials. Through MATLAB-COMSOL co-simulation, the PID controller maintains anode potentials above the lithium plating limit, achieving computationally efficient, model-based fast charging.
AI.motivation: Lithium plating during fast charging limits battery performance and safety when anode potential drops below 0 V vs Li/Li+. Model-based control needs to maximize charging current while preventing this, but high-fidelity models are computationally expensive for real-time control.
AI.method: A Homogenized Model (HM) derived from homogenization theory applied to Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations is coupled with a classical PID controller. The HM captures microstructural heterogeneity in a 1D double-continua formulation and reconstructs 3D electrochemical variable distributions from precomputed closure variables, acting as a virtual sensor. MATLAB-COMSOL co-simulation is used for implementation.
AI.result: The HM-based PID controller successfully regulates current to maintain the full 3D anode potential distribution above the lithium plating limit, achieving fast charging at significantly reduced computational cost compared to high-fidelity models.
AI.conclusion: HM-based control shows promise for safe, degradation-aware, and efficient fast charging of lithium-ion batteries by preventing lithium plating while being computationally practical.

title: A Distribution Matching Approach to Neural Piano Transcription with Optimal Transport
summary: This paper describes a novel paradigm that formalizes automatic piano transcription (APT) as an optimal transport (OT) problem, not as a frame-level multi-label binary classification problem. Our method learns to minimize the cost of transporting a predicted distribution of note events to the ground-truth distribution over time and frequency. The OT loss can thus accommodate temporal misalignment, leading to perceptually relevant optimization. We also propose a convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) with a harmonics-aware attention mechanism to capture the spectro-temporal dependencies inherent in music.Our experiments using the MAESTRO dataset showed that our method attained a state-of-the-art performance in onset detection. We confirmed the versatility of the OT loss in application to existing models.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel optimal transport (OT) based paradigm for automatic piano transcription (APT), replacing the conventional frame-level multi-label classification approach, and achieves state-of-the-art onset detection using a CRNN with harmonics-aware attention on the MAESTRO dataset.
AI.motivation: Traditional APT methods treat transcription as frame-level multi-label binary classification, which is sensitive to temporal misalignment and lacks perceptually relevant optimization. The authors aim to address these limitations by reformulating APT as an optimal transport problem.
AI.method: The method formalizes APT as an optimal transport (OT) problem, minimizing the cost of transporting a predicted note event distribution to the ground-truth distribution across time and frequency. A convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) with a harmonics-aware attention mechanism is proposed to capture spectro-temporal dependencies in music.
AI.result: Experiments on the MAESTRO dataset demonstrated state-of-the-art performance in onset detection. The OT loss was also shown to be versatile when applied to existing models.
AI.conclusion: The OT-based paradigm offers a perceptually relevant alternative to conventional classification-based APT, effectively handling temporal misalignment and improving onset detection accuracy. The OT loss is generalizable and can benefit other models.

title: Stable Fiber-Koopman Residual Dynamics for Environment-Constrained Robust Control
summary:
Learning-based dynamical models face a persistent tension between expressiveness and formal guarantees: richer model classes improve predictive accuracy, but their stability properties are typically verified only empirically, if at all.
  This paper proposes \emph{Stable Fiber-Koopman Residual Dynamics} (SFKD), a unified framework that simultaneously addresses environment-aware geometric consistency, latent-space stability certification, and bounded residual perturbation propagation.
  Concretely, SFKD constructs a fiber bundle latent manifold whose fibers encode environment-specific dynamics; an environment-conditioned Koopman operator governs the dominant linear evolution on each fiber; and a contraction-constrained residual neural network captures unmodeled nonlinear effects while admitting an explicit input-to-state stability (ISS) certificate.
  The resulting model is embedded in a sampling-based MPPI controller for autonomous vehicle path tracking under variable surface conditions and wind disturbances. Theoretical analysis establishes ISS of the latent dynamics and a finite ultimate bound on tracking error.
  Numerical experiments against five baselines -- Koopman MPC, Neural ODE, ICODE, ControlSynth, and ICODE-MPPI -- demonstrate a 31\% reduction in tracking RMSE, a 44\% improvement in control smoothness, and near-zero latent stability violation rate across environment-switching scenarios.

AI.tldr: SFKD combines fiber bundle latent manifolds, environment-conditioned Koopman operators, and contraction-constrained residual neural networks to provide certified stability and accurate predictions for autonomous vehicle path tracking under varying conditions, achieving 31% lower RMSE and 44% smoother control than baselines.
AI.motivation: Learning-based dynamical models suffer from a tension between expressiveness and formal guarantees; richer models improve accuracy but lack stability certification, relying only on empirical validation.
AI.method: SFKD constructs a fiber bundle latent manifold (fibers encode environment-specific dynamics), an environment-conditioned Koopman operator (dominant linear evolution per fiber), and a contraction-constrained residual neural network (unmodeled nonlinear effects with ISS certificate). The model is embedded in a sampling-based MPPI controller.
AI.result: 31% reduction in tracking RMSE, 44% improvement in control smoothness, near-zero latent stability violation rate across environment-switching scenarios, compared against Koopman MPC, Neural ODE, ICODE, ControlSynth, and ICODE-MPPI.
AI.conclusion: SFKD resolves the expressiveness-guarantees tension by providing provably stable latent dynamics (ISS certificate) and a finite ultimate bound on tracking error, validated numerically in autonomous vehicle path tracking under variable surface conditions and wind disturbances.

title: Profiling the Voice: Speaker-Specific Phoneme Fingerprinting for Speech Deepfake Detection
summary: The rapid advancement of generative AI has made audio deepfakes increasingly indistinguishable from authentic human vocals, posing significant threats to persons-of-interest (POI) such as public figures. Current detection systems primarily rely on generic, black-box models that fail to capture speaker-specific idiosyncratic traits and lack interpretability. In this paper, we propose Phoneme-based Voice Profiling (PVP), a novel personalized defense framework. By shifting the detection paradigm from macro-utterance analysis to micro-phonetic modeling, PVP captures the unique acoustic distributions underlying a POI's habitual articulatory patterns. Specifically, our framework models speaker-specific phonetic realizations using lightweight Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) estimated solely from bona fide reference speech. This design enables data-efficient profiling and robust generalization to previously unseen spoofing attacks without requiring heavy spoof-specific training. Furthermore, we introduce the first large-scale Chinese POI deepfake dataset to benchmark speaker-specific detection. Experimental results demonstrate that PVP significantly outperforms state-of-the-art generic detectors in POI spoofing scenarios, achieving substantial EER reductions while providing fine-grained, phoneme-level interpretability for forensic analysis. Code and data are available at: https://github.com/JunXue-tech/PVP

AI.tldr: Phoneme-based Voice Profiling (PVP) is a personalized defense framework against audio deepfakes targeting persons-of-interest. It uses Gaussian Mixture Models to capture speaker-specific phonetic patterns from bona fide speech, achieving superior detection performance and phoneme-level interpretability compared to generic black-box detectors.
AI.motivation: Audio deepfakes pose increasing threats to public figures, yet current detection systems rely on generic black-box models that fail to capture speaker-specific idiosyncratic traits and lack interpretability.
AI.method: PVP shifts detection from macro-utterance analysis to micro-phonetic modeling by estimating lightweight Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) from bona fide reference speech to capture a POI's habitual articulatory patterns. It also introduces the first large-scale Chinese POI deepfake dataset.
AI.result: PVP significantly outperforms state-of-the-art generic detectors in POI spoofing scenarios, achieving substantial Equal Error Rate (EER) reductions while providing fine-grained, phoneme-level interpretability.
AI.conclusion: Speaker-specific phonetic profiling via lightweight GMMs is an effective, data-efficient, and interpretable approach for defending against audio deepfakes targeting specific individuals.

title: Flexible Multi-Channel Target Speaker Extraction Using Geometry-Conditioned Spatially Selective Non-linear Filters
summary: Recently, a spatially selective non-linear filter (SSF) has been proposed for target speaker extraction, using the target direction-of-arrival (DOA) as a spatial cue. Since learned intermediate features are tied to the microphone geometry, the performance of the SSF degrades significantly when evaluated on mismatched array geometries. In this paper, we propose a geometry-conditioned SSF (GC-SSF), which incorporates a geometry-conditioning branch based on FiLM layers. Furthermore, we propose a feature that jointly encodes the DOA and the microphone positions (DOA-MPE). The conditioning branch modulates the intermediate feature maps of the SSF using the DOA-MPE feature to capture the spatial relationship between the microphone positions and the target speaker. Experimental results across circular, uniform linear, and random microphone arrays show that the proposed GC-SSF generalizes better to mismatched geometries while maintaining high spatial selectivity, demonstrating its ability to effectively adapt the filtering process to different array geometries

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Geometry-Conditioned Spatially Selective Filter (GC-SSF) that uses a geometry-conditioning branch with FiLM layers and a DOA-MPE feature to improve generalization across mismatched microphone array geometries for target speaker extraction.
AI.motivation: Standard SSF performance degrades significantly when evaluated on mismatched array geometries because learned intermediate features are tied to the microphone geometry.
AI.method: The proposed GC-SSF incorporates: (1) a geometry-conditioning branch based on FiLM layers, and (2) a DOA-MPE feature that jointly encodes the target DOA and microphone positions. The conditioning branch modulates intermediate feature maps using the DOA-MPE feature to capture spatial relationships.
AI.result: Across circular, uniform linear, and random microphone arrays, GC-SSF generalizes better to mismatched geometries while maintaining high spatial selectivity.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method effectively adapts the filtering process to different array geometries, demonstrating improved generalization capability.

title: A Coupled V2G Equilibrium Model of Electric Vehicle and Power System Interactions
summary: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology empowers electric vehicles (EVs) to act as mobile energy resources, providing critical support to power systems, especially under stressed conditions. To understand the economic mechanism driving V2G participation and its benefits to power grid, this paper proposes a multi-player coupled equilibrium framework that models the bidirectional interactions between power grid operations and EV routing, incorporating charging and discharging choice in a preprocessed feasible path generation procedure. Energy prices are endogenously determined by market clearance conditions. We formulate the overall problem as a Variational Inequality that unite the decision-making of Distribution System Operator, Charging Network Operator, Load Serving Entities, and EV drivers. Numerical studies validate the framework under two stress scenarios: increased household load and power line outages. Results show that when EVs are incentivized by reduced generalized path costs, V2G is particularly effective in eliminating load shedding and reducing distribution locational marginal electricity prices. On the transportation side, V2G can lead to divergence in EV behavior between normal and scarcity conditions, and alter route choices yet improve overall trip economic.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a multi-player coupled equilibrium framework using Variational Inequality to model bidirectional interactions between power grid operations and EV routing with V2G, showing that V2G effectively eliminates load shedding and reduces electricity prices under stress scenarios.
AI.motivation: To understand the economic mechanism driving V2G participation and its benefits to power systems, especially under stressed conditions such as increased household load and power line outages.
AI.method: A multi-player coupled equilibrium framework modeling bidirectional interactions between power grid operations and EV routing, incorporating charging/discharging choice in a preprocessed feasible path generation procedure, with energy prices endogenously determined by market clearance conditions; formulated as a Variational Inequality uniting DSO, CNO, LSEs, and EV drivers.
AI.result: V2G effectively eliminates load shedding and reduces distribution locational marginal electricity prices under stress scenarios; V2G causes divergence in EV behavior between normal and scarcity conditions and alters route choices while improving overall trip economics.
AI.conclusion: When incentivized by reduced generalized path costs, V2G provides significant economic and operational benefits to both power systems and transportation networks under stressed conditions.

title: Stable Audio 3
summary: Stable Audio 3 is a family of fast latent diffusion models (small, medium, large) for variable-length audio generation and editing. Since our models can generate several minutes of audio, variable-length generations are key to avoid the cost of producing full-length generations for short sounds. We also support inpainting, enabling targeted audio editing and the continuation of short recordings. Our latent diffusion models operate on top of a novel semantic-acoustic autoencoder that projects audio into a compact latent space, enabling efficient diffusion-based generation while preserving audio fidelity and encouraging semantic structure in the latent. Finally, we run adversarial post-training to both accelerate inference and improve generation quality, reducing the number of inference steps while improving fidelity and prompt adherence. Stable Audio 3 models are trained on licensed and Creative Commons data to generate music and sounds in less than a 2s on an H200 GPU and less than a few seconds on a MacBook Pro M4. We release the weights of small and medium, that can run on consumer-grade hardware, together with their training and inference pipeline.

AI.tldr: Stable Audio 3 introduces a family of variable-length latent diffusion models (small, medium, large) for efficient audio generation and editing, featuring a novel semantic-acoustic autoencoder, adversarial post-training, and support for inpainting, achieving high-quality audio generation in under 2 seconds on H200 GPU and releasing small/medium model weights.
AI.motivation: To enable variable-length audio generation without the computational cost of producing full-length generations for short sounds, and to support targeted audio editing via inpainting while maintaining efficiency and quality.
AI.method: Uses a family of fast latent diffusion models with a novel semantic-acoustic autoencoder for compact latent space projection, adversarial post-training for inference acceleration and quality improvement, and supports variable-length generation and inpainting.
AI.result: Generates music and sounds in under 2 seconds on an H200 GPU and within a few seconds on a MacBook Pro M4; releases small and medium model weights that run on consumer-grade hardware.
AI.conclusion: Stable Audio 3 achieves efficient, high-quality variable-length audio generation and editing with open-source availability for consumer-grade hardware.

title: Taming Audio VAEs via Target-KL Regularization
comment: Accepted at ICASSP 2026 (Barcelona, Spain, 3-8 May 2026). 5 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables
summary: Latent diffusion models have emerged as the dominant paradigm for many generation tasks including audio generation such as text-to-audio, text-to-music and text-to-speech. A key component of latent diffusion is an autoencoder (VAE) that compresses high-dimensional signals into a low frame rate continuous representation that is conducive for downstream prediction. Regularizing these VAEs is challenging, as there is a trade-off between over-regularized (poor output quality) and under-regularized (difficult to predict) latent representations. We propose a framework for studying this trade-off through compression and train Audio VAEs at specific bitrates via target-KL regularization. This allows direct comparison to well-studied discrete neural audio codec models, and the construction of rate-distortion curves for audio VAEs. We evaluate the impact of target-KL regularization on text-to-sound generation and find that sweeping compression rates is helpful in identifying the optimal generation setting.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a framework for regularizing audio VAEs in latent diffusion models via target-KL regularization to control compression bitrates, enabling rate-distortion analysis and identifying optimal settings for text-to-sound generation.
AI.motivation: Regularizing VAEs for latent diffusion models is challenging due to a trade-off between over-regularized (poor output quality) and under-regularized (difficult to predict) latent representations. The paper aims to systematically study this trade-off through compression.
AI.method: The authors propose training Audio VAEs with target-KL regularization to achieve specific bitrates, enabling direct comparison to discrete neural audio codec models and construction of rate-distortion curves for audio VAEs.
AI.result: Sweeping compression rates via target-KL regularization helps identify the optimal generation setting for text-to-sound generation tasks.
AI.conclusion: Target-KL regularization provides a principled way to control VAE compression rates, and exploring the rate-distortion trade-off is beneficial for finding the optimal balance in text-to-sound generation.

title: AoI-MDP: An AoI Optimized Markov Decision Process (Student Abstract)
summary: Ocean exploration places high demands on autonomous underwater vehicles, especially when there's observation delay. We propose age of information optimized Markov decision process (AoI-MDP) to enhance underwater tasks by modeling observation delay as signal delay and including it in the state space. AoI-MDP also introduces wait time in the action space and integrates AoI with reward functions, optimizing information freshness and decision-making using reinforcement learning. Simulations show AoI-MDP outperforms the standard MDP, demonstrating superior performance, feasibility, and generalization in underwater tasks. To accelerate relevant research, we have made the codes available as open-source at https://github.com/Xiboxtg/AoI-MDP.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes AoI-MDP, a framework that models observation delay as signal delay and incorporates Age of Information into the state space, action space, and reward function of Markov decision processes, optimized via reinforcement learning for better underwater autonomous vehicle task performance.
AI.motivation: Ocean exploration demands high performance from autonomous underwater vehicles, particularly when dealing with observation delay, which motivates the need for a framework that explicitly models and optimizes for information freshness.
AI.method: The method models observation delay as signal delay, includes it in the MDP state space, introduces wait time in the action space, and integrates Age of Information (AoI) into the reward function, then optimizes decision-making using reinforcement learning.
AI.result: Simulations show AoI-MDP outperforms the standard MDP, demonstrating superior performance, feasibility, and generalization across underwater tasks.
AI.conclusion: AoI-MDP effectively enhances decision-making for underwater vehicles under observation delay, and the authors have open-sourced the code to accelerate further research.

title: MusicDET: Zero-Shot AI-Generated Music Detection
summary: Detecting AI-generated music is crucial for preserving artistic authenticity and preventing the misuse of generative music technologies. However, existing discriminative detectors typically rely on generated samples during training and often suffer from severe performance degradation when confronted with music produced by unseen generators, which limits their real-world applicability. To address this issue, we formulate a zero-shot setting for AI-generated music detection, where the detector is trained exclusively on real music without access to any generated samples. Under this setting, we propose MusicDET, a generator-agnostic detection framework based on frequency-guided normalizing flows that probabilistically models the distribution of real music features. By evaluating the likelihood of an input sample under the learned real-music distribution, MusicDET enables effective detection of out-of-distribution music signals. Experiments on the FakeMusicCaps and SONICS datasets show that MusicDET consistently outperforms conventional discriminative detectors, particularly when detecting music generated by previously unseen models.

AI.tldr: MusicDET is a zero-shot AI-generated music detector using frequency-guided normalizing flows to model real music distributions, outperforming discriminative detectors on unseen generators.
AI.motivation: Existing discriminative AI-generated music detectors rely on generated samples during training and fail on music from unseen generators, limiting real-world applicability.
AI.method: Formulates a zero-shot detection setting where only real music is used for training. Proposes MusicDET, which uses frequency-guided normalizing flows to probabilistically model the distribution of real music features and detects out-of-distribution signals via likelihood evaluation.
AI.result: MusicDET consistently outperforms conventional discriminative detectors on FakeMusicCaps and SONICS datasets, especially for music generated by previously unseen models.
AI.conclusion: The proposed zero-shot, generator-agnostic approach effectively addresses the generalization issue in AI-generated music detection, offering practical advantages for real-world deployment.

title: Modeling Coincident Peak Pricing in Electricity Markets: Challenges and Peak Shaving Effectiveness
comment: Coincident Peak Pricing, Demand Response, Game Theory, Peak Shaving
summary: Coincident Peak (CP) pricing is widely used in U.S. electricity markets to allocate capacity and transmission costs. This paper develops a behavioral game-theoretic framework for CP-driven load shifting that couples a nonlinear cost-allocation model with day-ahead (one-shot) and real-time (sequential-learning) decision processes. We examine two update rules, namely best-response dynamics (BRD) and fictitious-play dynamics (FPD), across continuous and finite action spaces to quantify how flexibility, action resolution, and participation influence peak outcomes. Using ERCOT peak-day data, we find that FPD reliably reduces system peaks, whereas BRD is more variable and can increase peaks under tight-capacity conditions. Finer action resolution improves peak shaving, while the number of participants is largely neutral when aggregate flexibility is fixed. Meanwhile, information-provider signals can induce herding, whereas response-aware or diverse signals improve peak shaving. These results highlight both the potential and limits of CP pricing: smoothing information and enabling granular control are as important as the amount of available flexibility. The framework offers practical guidance for system operators and consumers: For ISOs, broadcasting smoothed CP signals and setting minimum controllable-capacity thresholds enhance coordination. For consumers, greater flexibility and finer control resolution improve both cost savings and peak-shaving performance.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a game-theoretic framework to analyze load shifting under Coincident Peak (CP) pricing, comparing best-response and fictitious-play dynamics. Using ERCOT data, it finds that fictitious-play dynamics reliably reduce system peaks, finer action resolution improves peak shaving, and information design matters more than participant count for coordination outcomes.
AI.motivation: CP pricing is widely used in U.S. electricity markets for cost allocation, but its strategic implications for load shifting and peak outcomes are not well understood theoretically or empirically.
AI.method: The authors develop a behavioral game-theoretic model coupling nonlinear cost allocation with day-ahead (one-shot) and real-time (sequential-learning) decision processes, examining best-response dynamics (BRD) and fictitious-play dynamics (FPD) across continuous and finite action spaces.
AI.result: FPD reliably reduces system peaks; BRD is more variable and can increase peaks under tight capacity. Finer action resolution improves peak shaving. Number of participants is neutral when aggregate flexibility is fixed. Information-provider signals can induce herding, while response-aware or diverse signals improve outcomes.
AI.conclusion: Smoothing information and enabling granular control are as important as the amount of available flexibility. For ISOs, broadcasting smoothed CP signals and setting minimum controllable-capacity thresholds enhance coordination. For consumers, greater flexibility and finer control resolution improve both cost savings and peak-shaving performance.

title: Sonalyzer-Moz: A Framework for Analyzing the Structure of Mozart's Sonata Form
summary: The sonata form is a musically rich and hierarchically structured form that poses significant challenges for automatic analysis. While music structure analysis has seen strides of progress in recent years, sonata form analysis remains in its early stages. This is largely due to the time-consuming and high barrier of the music background requirement for annotating classical music structures. To advance research in this area, we curated SoSA-Moz, the first large-scale dataset featuring comprehensive hierarchical structure annotations. This work establishes a foundation for systematic sonata form analysis. Leveraging this newly contributed resource, we further propose Sonalyzer-Moz, a baseline model specifically designed for investigating complex sonata structures. This framework integrates feature aggregation with sequential modeling, enabling it to capture both local feature and upper-level structural dependencies. Experiment results show that Sonalyzer-Moz is capable of identifying the components' boundaries of the upper-level structure that are critical to understanding sonata form. Therefore, this method demonstrates, for the first time, the effectiveness of automatic upper-level analysis of sonata form, and provides a robust baseline for future research in the automatic understanding of sonata form while advancing the study of classical music structure analysis.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces SoSA-Moz, the first large-scale dataset with hierarchical structure annotations for sonata form analysis, and proposes Sonalyzer-Moz, a baseline model integrating feature aggregation and sequential modeling to automatically identify upper-level structural boundaries in sonata form.
AI.motivation: Sonata form analysis remains challenging and underdeveloped due to the lack of large-scale annotated datasets and the high barrier of music expertise required for annotation, hindering progress in automatic classical music structure analysis.
AI.method: The authors curated SoSA-Moz, a large-scale dataset with comprehensive hierarchical structure annotations. They then developed Sonalyzer-Moz, a baseline model that integrates feature aggregation with sequential modeling to capture both local features and upper-level structural dependencies for sonata form analysis.
AI.result: Sonalyzer-Moz effectively identifies component boundaries of the upper-level structure critical to understanding sonata form, demonstrating the first successful automatic upper-level analysis of sonata form.
AI.conclusion: This work provides the first large-scale dataset and a robust baseline model for automatic sonata form analysis, advancing the field of classical music structure analysis and enabling future research in automatic understanding of sonata form.

title: SIREM: Speech-Informed MRI Reconstruction with Learned Sampling
summary: Real-time magnetic resonance imaging (rtMRI) of speech production enables non-invasive visualization of dynamic vocal-tract motion and is valuable for speech science and clinical assessment. However, rtMRI is fundamentally constrained by trade-offs among spatial resolution, temporal resolution, and acquisition speed, often leading to undersampled k-space measurements and degraded reconstructions. We propose SIREM, a speech-informed MRI reconstruction framework that uses synchronized speech as a cross-modal prior. The central idea is that vocal-tract configurations during speech are correlated with the produced acoustics, making part of the image content predictable from audio. SIREM models each frame as a fusion of an audio-driven component and an MRI-driven component through a spatial weighting map. The audio branch predicts articulator-related structure from speech, while the MRI branch reconstructs complementary content from measured k-space data. We further introduce a learnable soft weighting profile over spiral arms, enabling a differentiable study of how k-space arm usage interacts with speech-informed fusion. This yields a unified multimodal formulation that combines audio-driven prediction, MRI reconstruction, and sampling adaptation. We evaluate SIREM on the USC speech rtMRI benchmark against standard baselines, including gridding, wavelet-based compressed sensing, and total variation. SIREM introduces a speech-informed reconstruction paradigm that operates in a substantially higher-throughput regime than iterative methods while preserving anatomically plausible vocal-tract structure. These results establish an initial benchmark for multimodal speech-informed rtMRI reconstruction and highlight the potential of synchronized speech as an auxiliary prior for fast reconstruction. The source code is available at https://github.com/mdhasanai/SIREM

AI.tldr: SIREM is a speech-informed MRI reconstruction framework that uses synchronized audio as a cross-modal prior to improve real-time MRI of speech production, achieving faster and anatomically plausible reconstructions by fusing audio-driven and MRI-driven components via spatial weighting maps and learnable k-space sampling.
AI.motivation: Real-time MRI of speech production suffers from inherent trade-offs between spatial resolution, temporal resolution, and acquisition speed, leading to undersampled k-space measurements and degraded reconstructions. The authors aim to leverage synchronized speech audio as an auxiliary prior to improve reconstruction quality.
AI.method: SIREM decomposes each frame into an audio-driven component (predicting articulator-related structures from speech) and an MRI-driven component (reconstructing complementary content from k-space data), merged via a spatial weighting map. A learnable soft weighting profile over spiral arms enables differentiable optimization of sampling trajectory jointly with reconstruction.
AI.result: Evaluated on the USC speech rtMRI benchmark, SIREM outperforms gridding, wavelet-based compressed sensing, and total variation baselines. It operates in a substantially higher-throughput regime than iterative methods while preserving anatomically plausible vocal-tract structure.
AI.conclusion: SIREM establishes an initial benchmark for multimodal speech-informed rtMRI reconstruction and demonstrates that synchronized speech is an effective auxiliary prior for fast, high-quality reconstruction.

title: A Resilience Evaluation Framework for Electric Distribution Systems: Historical Weather Conditioning, Sensitivity Analysis, and a Flooding-Aware Extension
comment: Submitted to International Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems
summary: Evaluating resilience in electric distribution systems under severe weather requires models that can connect network topology, hazard simulation, fragility modeling, restoration assumptions, repair strategy, and downstream consequences. This paper extends our prior graph-based resilience evaluation framework for power distribution systems in three ways: it adds analysis conditioned on historical events with real outage and weather data, introduces sensitivity studies for key modeling assumptions, and includes a coupled power-flooding extension for sewage-backup assessment. Historical wind events drive Monte Carlo simulations conditioned on real weather, and the observed outage trajectories are treated as realized historical samples for comparison. Wind-event resilience metrics stabilize at approximately 256 episodes, and outage peak, duration, and outage intensity change systematically with fragility parameters, network topology, restoration assumptions, and repair strategies. In a separate 1000-episode joint power-flooding simulation, episodes with at least one flooded customer occur in 1.9% of episodes overall, and both flood occurrence and flood intensity increase with outage intensity, showing a selective power-to-flood consequence pathway. Overall, the framework provides a practical basis for resilience assessment, comparative scenario analysis, and coupled power-flooding studies in a limited public-data setting, while also suggesting that more detailed utility data could further improve simulation realism.

AI.tldr: This paper extends a graph-based resilience evaluation framework for power distribution systems by incorporating historical event conditioning with real outage/weather data, sensitivity studies on key modeling assumptions, and a coupled power-flooding extension for sewage-backup assessment. Wind-event resilience metrics stabilize at ~256 episodes; parameters like fragility, topology, restoration, and repair strategies systematically affect resilience outcomes. In 1000-episode joint simulations, 1.9% show flooded customers, with flood occurrence and intensity increasing with outage intensity.
AI.motivation: To develop a comprehensive resilience evaluation framework for electric distribution systems under severe weather that can integrate network topology, hazard simulation, fragility modeling, restoration assumptions, repair strategies, and downstream consequences, while also enabling joint power-flooding assessment.
AI.method: Extension of a prior graph-based resilience evaluation framework with three additions: (1) historical event conditioning using real outage and weather data, (2) sensitivity studies for key modeling assumptions, (3) coupled power-flooding extension for sewage-backup assessment. Wind events use Monte Carlo simulations conditioned on real weather; joint power-flooding simulations run for 1000 episodes.
AI.result: Wind-event resilience metrics stabilize at approximately 256 episodes. Outage peak, duration, and intensity vary systematically with fragility, topology, restoration assumptions, and repair strategies. In 1000-episode joint power-flooding simulations, 1.9% of episodes have at least one flooded customer; flood occurrence and intensity increase with outage intensity.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a practical basis for resilience assessment, comparative scenario analysis, and coupled power-flooding studies in a limited public-data setting, though access to more detailed utility data could further improve simulation realism.

title: EnvTriCascade: An Environment-Aware Tri-Stage Cascaded Framework for ESDD2 2026 Challenge
summary: ADD in real-world scenarios has evolved from speech-only spoofing to more challenging component-level settings, where speech and environmental sounds may be independently manipulated. To tackle this, we propose EnvTriCascade, an Environment-Aware Tri-Stage Cascaded framework for the ESDD2 Challenge. First, a mix-consistency detector provides a binary prior to distinguish original recordings from manipulated mixtures, which calibrates the final decisions. Next, two complementary five-class detectors, leveraging SSLAM+XLS-R and EAT-large+XLS-R representations, extract robust multi-branch features integrated via a cross-branch attention-gated classifier. To enhance robustness against diverse mixing conditions, we incorporate RawBoost augmentation. Trained exclusively on the official CompSpoofV2 dataset, our system achieves a Macro-F1 score of 0.8266 on the test set, significantly outperforming the official baseline and ranking second in the challenge.

AI.tldr: EnvTriCascade, an Environment-Aware Tri-Stage Cascaded framework, ranks second in the ESDD2 Challenge by detecting component-level audio deepfakes (speech + environmental sounds) using a mix-consistency detector, complementary multi-branch SSL features, and RawBoost augmentation, achieving 0.8266 Macro-F1.
AI.motivation: Audio deepfake detection (ADD) has evolved from speech-only spoofing to more challenging component-level manipulation, where speech and environmental sounds may be independently tampered with, necessitating a robust detection framework.
AI.method: A three-stage cascaded pipeline: (1) a mix-consistency detector provides binary prior distinguishing original vs. manipulated mixtures; (2) two complementary five-class detectors using SSLAM+XLS-R and EAT-large+XLS-R extract multi-branch features; (3) a cross-branch attention-gated classifier fuses features, with RawBoost augmentation for robustness.
AI.result: Achieves Macro-F1 of 0.8266 on the ESDD2 Challenge test set, significantly outperforming the official baseline and ranking second place.
AI.conclusion: The proposed environment-aware multi-stage framework effectively addresses component-level audio spoofing detection by leveraging complementary SSL representations and consistency priors.

title: SAME: A Semantically-Aligned Music Autoencoder
summary: Latent representations are at the heart of the majority of modern generative models. In the audio domain they are typically produced by a neural-audio-codec autoencoder. In this work we introduce SAME (Semantically-Aligned Music autoEncoder), an autoencoder for stereo music and general audio that reaches a 4096$\times$ temporal compression ratio while maintaining reconstruction quality and downstream generative performance. We achieve this by combining a tranformer-based backbone with set of semantic regularisation approaches, phase-aware reconstruction losses and improved discriminator designs. The architecture delivers substantial computational cost benefits, through both its high compression ratio and its reliance on well-optimised transformer primitives. Two variants (a large SAME-L and a CPU-deployable SAME-S) are released in open-weights form.

AI.tldr: SAME is a neural audio codec autoencoder that achieves 4096× temporal compression for stereo music while maintaining quality, using transformers, semantic regularization, phase-aware losses, and improved discriminators.
AI.motivation: To achieve extreme temporal compression (4096×) for stereo music and general audio without sacrificing reconstruction quality or downstream generative performance, while reducing computational costs.
AI.method: Combines a transformer-based backbone with semantic regularization approaches, phase-aware reconstruction losses, and improved discriminator designs to produce semantically-aligned latent representations.
AI.result: Achieves 4096× temporal compression ratio with maintained reconstruction quality and downstream generative performance, with two open-weight variants (SAME-L and SAME-S).
AI.conclusion: SAME demonstrates that extreme compression ratios are feasible for stereo music while preserving quality, enabled by transformer architectures and tailored regularization/loss strategies.

title: Empirical evaluation of Time Series Foundation Models for Day-ahead and Imbalance Electricity Price Forecasting in Belgium
summary: Recent advances in Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) promise zero-shot forecasting capabilities with minimal task-specific training. While these models have shown strong performance across generic benchmarks, their applicability in volatile, complex electricity markets remains underexplored. Addressing this gap, this study provides a systematic empirical evaluation of several TSFMs, specifically Chronos-2 and Chronos-Bolt (developed by Amazon), and TimesFM 2.5 (provided by Google), for forecasting Belgian day-ahead and imbalance electricity prices. For both considered markets, Chronos-2 in ARX mode produces the most accurate forecasts. Compared with the best ensemble prediction from other machine learning methods, Chronos-2's Mean Absolute Error (MAE) is 5% lower for the day-ahead market. In contrast, the model yields 10% higher MAE predicting imbalance prices across all forecast horizons, except for the two-hour-ahead horizon. Moreover, we find that TSFMs exhibit genuine zero-shot forecasting skills but still struggle under extreme market conditions.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates Time Series Foundation Models (Chronos-2, Chronos-Bolt, TimesFM 2.5) for forecasting Belgian electricity prices. Chronos-2 in ARX mode performs best, achieving 5% lower MAE than ML ensembles for day-ahead prices but 10% higher MAE for imbalance prices. TSFMs show zero-shot capabilities but struggle under extreme market conditions.
AI.motivation: To bridge the gap between the proven zero-shot forecasting capabilities of TSFMs on generic benchmarks and their underexplored applicability in volatile, complex electricity markets.
AI.method: Systematic empirical evaluation of Chronos-2, Chronos-Bolt, and TimesFM 2.5 for forecasting Belgian day-ahead and imbalance electricity prices, with comparison against ensemble ML methods.
AI.result: Chronos-2 in ARX mode achieves 5% lower MAE than best ML ensemble for day-ahead prices, but 10% higher MAE for imbalance prices. TSFMs demonstrate genuine zero-shot skills but struggle under extreme conditions.
AI.conclusion: TSFMs are viable for electricity price forecasting but have limitations in handling extreme market volatility; further research is needed to improve robustness.

title: WavFlow: Audio Generation in Waveform Space
summary: Modern audio generation predominantly relies on latent-space compression, introducing additional complexity and potential information loss. In this work, we challenge this paradigm with WavFlow, a framework that generates high-fidelity audio directly in raw waveform space without intermediate representations. To overcome the inherent difficulties of modeling high-dimensional and low-energy signals, we reshape audio into 2D token grids through waveform patchify and introduce amplitude lifting to align signal scales, enabling stable optimization via direct x-prediction in flow matching. To capture complex semantic alignment and temporal synchronization, we leverage an automated data pipeline to curate 5 million high-quality video-text-audio triplets, allowing the model to learn fine-grained acoustic patterns from scratch. Experimental results show that WavFlow achieves competitive performance on the video-to-audio benchmark VGGSound (FD_PaSST: 59.98, IS_PANNs: 17.40, DeSync: 0.44) and the text-to-audio benchmark AudioCaps (FD_PANNs: 10.63, IS_PANNs: 12.62), matching or exceeding the performance of established latent-based methods. Our work demonstrates that intermediate compression is not a prerequisite for high-quality synthesis, offering a simpler and more scalable alternative for multimodal audio generation.

AI.tldr: WavFlow generates high-fidelity audio directly in raw waveform space using flow matching, avoiding latent-space compression. It reshapes audio into 2D token grids via waveform patchify, uses amplitude lifting for stable optimization, and is trained on 5M video-text-audio triplets. It achieves competitive results on VGGSound and AudioCaps, showing intermediate compression is unnecessary for high-quality synthesis.
AI.motivation: Existing audio generation relies on latent-space compression, which introduces complexity and potential information loss. The authors challenge this paradigm by exploring direct raw waveform generation.
AI.method: (1) Waveform patchify to reshape audio into 2D token grids. (2) Amplitude lifting to align signal scales for stable optimization. (3) Direct x-prediction in flow matching. (4) Automated data pipeline to curate 5M video-text-audio triplets for learning fine-grained acoustic patterns.
AI.result: VGGSound: FD_PaSST=59.98, IS_PANNs=17.40, DeSync=0.44. AudioCaps: FD_PANNs=10.63, IS_PANNs=12.62. Matches or exceeds latent-based methods.
AI.conclusion: Intermediate compression is not a prerequisite for high-quality audio synthesis. Direct waveform generation is a simpler and more scalable alternative for multimodal audio generation.

title: Ensuring reliability in 100% renewable microgrids: a scenario-based joint planning and operational design framework
comment: Accepted by Energy Conversion and Management on 13 May 2026
summary: Off-grid microgrids powered entirely by renewable energy sources face substantial challenges in achieving utility-grade reliability standards. Existing microgrid planning frameworks often prioritize cost minimization while treating reliability as a secondary metric, thereby leading to suboptimal designs. This paper presents a comprehensive scenario-based optimization framework that simultaneously addresses long-term capacity planning and short-term operational dispatch in two stages for 100%-renewable microgrids. The developed two-stage stochastic programming model co-optimizes the investment and operation of photovoltaic generation and battery energy storage, while ensuring compliance with stringent reliability constraints following utility grid standards. Network modeling with operational constraints, such as line capacities and voltage limits, is incorporated to allow distributed resource placement leveraging power sharing between microgrid nodes. A novel scenario generation approach captures critical uncertainties, including seasonal demand fluctuations, solar output variations, and probabilistic equipment failures, through the statistical clustering of historical data. The optimization framework integrates utility-grade reliability constraints limiting the expected energy not served to below 0.002% of the annual demand while minimizing the total system costs. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, achieving 99.998% supply reliability using only photovoltaic power and battery energy storage. The optimized network-aware distributed resource allocation provides inherent resilience through power rerouting during component outages, maintaining load continuity even under simultaneous equipment failures. This study confirms the feasibility of 100%-renewable microgrids to support remote communities while meeting utility-grade reliability benchmarks.

AI.tldr: A two-stage stochastic optimization framework for 100%-renewable microgrids that co-optimizes photovoltaic and battery capacity planning with operational dispatch, achieving 99.998% supply reliability under utility-grade constraints through network-aware distributed resource allocation and scenario-based uncertainty modeling.
AI.motivation: Off-grid renewable microgrids struggle to meet utility-grade reliability standards because existing planning frameworks prioritize cost minimization over reliability, resulting in suboptimal designs that fail to ensure dependable power supply for remote communities.
AI.method: A two-stage stochastic programming model is developed that co-optimizes long-term capacity planning (PV generation and battery storage) and short-term operational dispatch. It incorporates network modeling (line capacities, voltage limits), a novel scenario generation approach using statistical clustering of historical data for uncertainties (seasonal demand, solar output, equipment failures), and utility-grade reliability constraints limiting expected energy not served to below 0.002% of annual demand.
AI.result: The framework achieves 99.998% supply reliability using only PV and battery storage, with network-aware distributed resource allocation providing inherent resilience through power rerouting during component outages, maintaining load continuity even under simultaneous equipment failures.
AI.conclusion: The study confirms that 100%-renewable microgrids can feasibly support remote communities while meeting utility-grade reliability benchmarks through co-optimized planning and network-aware design.

title: FSD50K-Solo: Automated Curation of Single-Source Sound Events
summary: High-quality training datasets are essential for the performance of neural networks. However, the audio domain still lacks a large-scale, strongly-labeled, and single-source sound event dataset. The FSD50K dataset, despite being relatively large and open, contains a considerable fraction of multi-source samples where background interference or overlapping events could limit the usefulness of the data. To address this challenge, we introduce a data curation framework designed for large-scale open audio corpora. Our approach leverages a generative diffusion model to synthesize clean single-class events to construct controlled noisy mixtures for supervision. We subsequently employ a pre-trained audio encoder coupled with a discriminative classifier to automatically identify and filter out multi-source samples. Experiments show that our framework achieves strong performance on a human expert-curated test set. Finally, we release FSD50K-Solo, a model-curated subset of FSD50K containing single-source audio samples identified by our method. Beyond FSD50K, our method establishes a scalable paradigm for curating open source audio corpora.

AI.tldr: Introduces a data curation framework using generative diffusion models and discriminative classifiers to identify and filter multi-source samples from large audio corpora, resulting in FSD50K-Solo—a single-source subset of FSD50K.
AI.motivation: High-quality single-source strongly-labeled audio datasets are lacking; existing datasets like FSD50K contain many multi-source samples (background interference, overlapping events) that limit utility.
AI.method: (1) Use a generative diffusion model to synthesize clean single-class events and construct controlled noisy mixtures. (2) Train a discriminative classifier with a pre-trained audio encoder on these mixtures. (3) Apply the classifier to automatically identify and filter multi-source samples from FSD50K.
AI.result: Strong performance on a human expert-curated test set; release of FSD50K-Solo, a model-curated single-source subset of FSD50K.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a scalable paradigm for curating open-source audio corpora beyond FSD50K.

title: A review of imbalance price forecasting algorithms in Europe: algorithms, metrics and the way forward
summary: Renewable electricity generation has grown significantly across many European power systems, leading to a greener energy mix, but also additional complexity in balancing electricity supply and demand. Unexpected differences between forecasts and actual output can lead to fluctuations in the system imbalance, which causes volatile imbalance prices. Accurate imbalance price forecasts are crucial for market players to choose a strategic balancing position. In early works, most forecasting methods combined fundamental and statistical approaches, but currently there is a clear trend towards data-driven machine learning models. This review compares forecasting algorithms in European markets with a focus on methodology. We emphasize the importance of high-quality input data, including intraday information and per-minute system data. Next, we identify the need for a common benchmark to compare novel forecasting methods developed for different markets and time periods. Finally, we argue that forecasts should be evaluated in terms of both downstream value and accuracy.

AI.tldr: A review comparing forecasting algorithms for imbalance prices in European power systems, highlighting the shift from fundamental-statistical approaches to data-driven machine learning models, and identifying key needs: high-quality intraday/minutely data, common benchmarks, and evaluation based on both downstream value and accuracy.
AI.motivation: The growth of renewable electricity generation increases complexity in balancing supply and demand, causing volatile imbalance prices. Accurate imbalance price forecasts are essential for market players to determine strategic balancing positions.
AI.method: A comparative review of forecasting algorithms used in European markets, focusing on methodology; examining input data quality (including intraday and per-minute system data), the need for common benchmarks, and evaluation metrics.
AI.result: Identifies a clear trend from fundamental-statistical methods toward data-driven machine learning models; emphasizes the necessity of high-quality input data; finds a lack of common benchmarks for cross-market comparison; argues for evaluating forecasts on both downstream value and accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Future work should prioritize common benchmarks for comparing novel forecasting methods across markets and time periods, and adopt dual evaluation criteria (accuracy and downstream value) for imbalance price forecasts.

title: Robust Audio Tagging under Class-wise Supervision Unreliability
summary: Weakly labeled datasets such as AudioSet have driven recent progress in audio tagging. However, annotation quality varies across sound classes. Labels may be incomplete, ambiguous, or unreliable, which introduces class-dependent supervision bias during optimisation. The issue becomes harder as real and generated audio are increasingly mixed in training, and generated samples do not always match their intended semantic labels. Prior work mainly addressed unreliable supervision from missing-positive labels, while this paper targets three other sources of unreliable supervision: spurious additions, misassignments between similar classes, and weakened label evidence. These effects introduce class-dependent optimisation bias that is not explicitly modeled by most existing methods. To bridge this gap, the paper proposes a Class-wise Supervision Unreliability (CSU) framework that controls supervision strength at the class level during training. CSU learns a separate unreliability parameter for each class and down-weights less reliable supervision without changing the model architecture or inference process. To support evaluations, this paper also introduces ESC-FreeGen50, a manually verified benchmark of 50 sound classes that combines real and generated audio. Experiments on controlled benchmarks and AudioSet show that CSU improves robustness across different architectures and different sources of supervision unreliability. The results indicate that explicit class-wise modeling of supervision unreliability is an effective and practical strategy for robust audio tagging under large-scale weakly labeled training. Code and data are available at: https://github.com/Yuanbo2020/CSU

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Class-wise Supervision Unreliability (CSU) framework that learns per-class unreliability parameters to down-weight unreliable supervision from spurious additions, misassignments, and weakened label evidence in weakly labeled audio datasets, improving robustness across architectures without changing model inference.
AI.motivation: Weakly labeled audio datasets like AudioSet have annotation quality issues (incomplete, ambiguous, unreliable labels) that introduce class-dependent supervision bias. Prior work mainly addressed missing-positive labels, but three other sources of unreliability—spurious additions, misassignments between similar classes, and weakened label evidence—remain unmodeled, causing optimization bias.
AI.method: CSU learns a separate unreliability parameter for each sound class and down-weights less reliable supervision during training at the class level, without changing model architecture or inference. The paper also introduces ESC-FreeGen50, a manually verified benchmark of 50 sound classes combining real and generated audio for evaluation.
AI.result: Experiments on controlled benchmarks and AudioSet show CSU improves robustness across different architectures and different sources of supervision unreliability.
AI.conclusion: Explicit class-wise modeling of supervision unreliability is an effective and practical strategy for robust audio tagging under large-scale weakly labeled training.

title: Geometric Fault Identification via Mirror Descent Learning
summary: This paper develops a fault detection and identification (FDI) method for nonlinear control-affine systems under simultaneous actuator and sensor faults. We adopt a geometric approach to study the isolability of faults in the sense of the principal angles between subspaces corresponding to each actuator and sensor fault. As for the fault identification, a hybrid estimator that consists of a Luenberger-like observer with contraction guarantees is developed. Moreover, neural networks are embedded in the mentioned observer to estimate actuator and sensor faults. Considering that the training dataset for neural networks cannot be representative of every fault scenario, the last layer of each network is adapted using mirror descent-based laws. The mirror descent-based adaptive laws impose isolability conditions for fault channels and do not assume a quadratic parameter estimation space to consider the geometry of the fault subspaces. A Lyapunov-based analysis establishes that the state and parameter estimation errors are uniformly ultimately bounded. The effectiveness of our proposed FDI method is illustrated on the 3-axis attitude control system of a spacecraft.

AI.tldr: A geometric FDI method for nonlinear control-affine systems with simultaneous actuator and sensor faults, using principal angles for fault isolability, a Luenberger-like observer with neural networks for fault identification, and mirror descent-based adaptive laws for online neural network adaptation.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of simultaneous actuator and sensor fault detection and identification in nonlinear control-affine systems, where traditional methods may struggle with fault isolability and the non-representative nature of training datasets for neural network-based estimators.
